rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Introduces a new timing/execution obligation for multi-unit franchisees: simultaneous signing of the first-shop Franchise Agreement with the DRA.

4 atomic changes. Imposes a minimum 2-shop development commitment, increasing franchisee obligation. Introduces a new right for franchisor to require reimbursement up to $2,000 for certain site visits, adding potential cost to franchisee.

7 atomic changes. New right allows franchisor to modify revenue recognition and Gross Sales definition, affecting the base for percentage fees. New fee introduced allowing franchisor to require reimbursement for resolving customer complaints if franchisee fails to do so.

6 atomic changes. Estimated FF&E initial investment for Commissary location increased from $75k-$90k to $125k-$140k. Estimated FF&E initial investment for Drive-Thru location increased from $85k-$105k to $115k-$135k.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. Material expansion of the categories of entities that may be designated or approved, increasing franchisor control over sourcing. New explicit disclaimer of reimbursement for loyalty-program costs, a material economic condition allocating costs to the franchisee.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. Franchisor data access expanded to continuous access to all operational information with explicit absence of contractual limitations. New mandatory $10,000 minimum spend on market introduction program is a material new franchisee obligation.

2 atomic changes. New explicit franchisee duty to follow franchisor instructions in copyright proceedings. New contractual limitation on franchisee's rights to copyrighted items after franchisor-required modification or discontinuance.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. The development-rights non-curable default list is materially expanded to include failure to cure a written default notice, cessation of operations, and Approved Affiliate conduct. New disclosure specifies that franchisee loses all development rights upon termination or expiration, a clear economic consequence.
4 atomic changes. Clear change in the stated data source for the FPR. Clear change in the inclusion/exclusion rule for the FPR.
1 atomic change. Disclosure method changed from aggregate-only to state-specific transfer reporting.

2 atomic changes. Removal of the unaudited interim balance sheet is a clear disclosure-coverage change in Item 21. Removal of the unaudited interim profit and loss statement is a clear disclosure-coverage change in Item 21.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Approved Affiliate ownership threshold may be reduced from 75% to as low as 51% at franchisor discretion. Addition of Blackstone-affiliated franchise program disclosures; expands affiliate disclosure scope.
1 atomic change. Material increase in the disclosed upper bound of the affiliate modular building price range, with lower bound unchanged.
1 atomic change. Material increase in the estimated Building/Build-Out Costs range (lower +$3,000, upper +$86,000) disclosed in Item 7.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. New disclosed revenue stream from technology subscription services reimbursement appears for the first time. New exception changes the scope of the franchisor's direct contracting for technology subscription services.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Brand Fund permissible expenditure scope expanded to explicitly include preopening support and franchisee training.

3 atomic changes. New disclaimer that the franchisor has no obligation to resolve territory/customer conflicts with affiliated systems, shifting potential risk to the franchisee. New discretionary right-of-first-refusal for Non-Traditional stores, changing the prior absolute statement that the franchisee has no right to develop such stores under the DRR.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. New disclosure that the franchisor often waives or limits the personal guarantee is a material change in the disclosed enforceability of a major obligation.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Adds a new conditional ground for franchisee termination based on an unspecified EBITDA threshold, materially altering the franchisee's exit rights.

3 atomic changes. The number of company-owned stores in the FPR sample changed materially from 13 to 16, altering the composition of the performance representation. The royalty treatment of company-owned stores in the FPR changed from not paying to paying royalties, materially altering the reported EBITDA figures.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 7 atomic changes. New commission structure creates a payment obligation from franchisor to Area Representatives, a material economic change. The franchisor's disclosed business scope expands from SUCCESS Space franchises only to also include Area Representative Businesses, a material change in the lines of business.
1 atomic change. New Item 4 specifies a disclosure location for Area Representative bankruptcy in Exhibit G, a clear disclosure-method change while the general no-bankruptcy statement remains.

6 atomic changes. The default obligation for conference attendance shifts from franchisor-designated optional or mandatory to mandatory unless waived, changing the franchisee's attendance obligation. A new conditional limitation on franchisor's post-termination lost-profits claim is introduced, reducing potential franchisee liability.

2 atomic changes. New mandatory reporting obligation imposed on franchisee after opening. Removal of explicit exclusion of percentage-based fees changes the definition of what is included in the Additional Funds estimate.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. The required minimum coverage for business interruption insurance changed from a time-based minimum to a sales- or loss-based formula. The notification method changed from a broad list including verbal/telephonic to email, Manual updates, or other means.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. Introduction of a new ongoing fee for Cafe POS system, a material additional franchisee cost. Addition of noncompliance fees to the Brand Fund deposits, introducing a new potential fee category.

6 atomic changes. Expands affiliate's right to operate Limited Services Facilities into development territory, reducing franchisee's territorial protection. New explicit $2,500 relocation fee imposes a material additional cost on franchisees.
1 atomic change. New mandatory confidentiality agreement execution requirement before access to confidential information is a clear operational/control change and a contractual obligation.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. New explicit financial guarantee obligation for owners/spouses is a material economic condition change.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 14 atomic changes. Narrowing the ADA cross-termination trigger reduces franchisor ability to terminate the ADA for any FA termination. Narrowing the ADA termination exception expands franchisor ability to terminate a good-standing FA for ADA defaults.
1 atomic change. Clear disclosure-method change in granularity from aggregate-only to state-level reporting.

1 atomic change. The franchisor removed the previously disclosed unaudited interim balance sheet and profit and loss statements from Item 21, a clear change in the financial disclosure provided to prospective franchisees.

rows.company: Pure Sweat Suana Studio, Pure Sweat & Float Studio
rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The scope of approved services and the service-format categories that determine the Studio brand changed, including removal of the sauna-only format and introduction of 'contrast therapy' as a defined format.

rows.company: Pure Sweat Suana Studio, Pure Sweat & Float Studio
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Clear operational change in the stated location where initial training may be provided, giving the franchisor discretion to use a designated studio instead of corporate headquarters.

rows.company: Pure Sweat Suana Studio, Pure Sweat & Float Studio
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Technology fee current charge changed from a flat per-user fee to a base plus per-email-user fee. An annual 25% increase cap was added to the additional employee initial training fee.

rows.company: Pure Sweat Suana Studio, Pure Sweat & Float Studio
rows.summary: 11 atomic changes. Both the low and high ends of the equipment estimate increased, a material change in estimated costs. Both the low and high ends of the furniture and fixtures estimate increased, a material change in estimated costs.

rows.company: Pure Sweat Suana Studio, Pure Sweat & Float Studio
rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Introduction of a new franchisor approval right over all FF&E selections, increasing franchisor control. Restriction of the supplier universe for unbranded FF&E from any supplier to only those on the franchisor's designated lists, a material sourcing restriction.

rows.company: Pure Sweat Suana Studio, Pure Sweat & Float Studio
rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. Adds a mandatory price-menu compliance obligation, materially shifting pricing control from franchisee discretion toward franchisor direction. Expands franchisor discretion over initial training venue from corporate/headquarters/Nashville to any studio designated by the franchisor.

rows.company: Pure Sweat Suana Studio, Pure Sweat & Float Studio
rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Litigation forum expanded from State court within or closest to Davidson County to also include Federal Court and the court nearest to the franchisor's corporate headquarters, materially changing the forum selection. Venue for mandatory mediation and arbitration expanded from Davidson County only to also include the nearest suitable location to the franchisor's corporate headquarters, materially altering the dispute resolution forum.

rows.company: Pure Sweat Sauna Studio, Pure Sweat & Float Studio
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Addition of summary statistics changes the presentation of financial performance data. Expansion of Utilization Rate definition to include contrast therapy changes the metric's scope.

rows.company: Pure Sweat Suana Studio, Pure Sweat & Float Studio
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Clear disclosure-method change: the cutoff date for projected openings shifted from December 31, 2024 to September 30, 2025. Clear disclosure-method change: the franchisor now discloses that some franchisees have signed confidentiality clauses, whereas previously it stated none had.

rows.company: Pure Sweat Suana Studio, Pure Sweat & Float Studio
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. New disclosure of unaudited interim financial statements; a disclosure-method change with no economic burden.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Fundamental change in the franchise offering from single-unit to Area Representative. Removal of a substantive disclosure section about industry-specific laws.

6 atomic changes. Fundamental restructuring from a flat single-location fee to a per-territory fee with negotiation for developed territories. Introduction of a conditional refund right that reduces franchisee risk.

20 atomic changes. Removal of the minimum royalty schedule is a fundamental restructuring of the royalty fee. Removal of the primary royalty fee is a fundamental restructuring of the economic relationship.

16 atomic changes. Fundamental restructuring from single franchise to Area Representative Territory changes the entire investment estimate. Material change in the initial franchise fee amount and structure from flat to range.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 16 atomic changes. Adds deemed approval after 30 days for alternative suppliers. Adds termination right for noncompliance with supplier standards.

2 atomic changes. The obligated party changes from franchisee to area representative and the governing agreement changes from Franchise Agreement to Area Representative Agreement, indicating a fundamental change in the economic relationship. The maintenance, appearance and remodeling requirement changes from having a section reference in the agreement to Not Applicable, indicating the obligation is no longer imposed.

7 atomic changes. Removal of a discretionary franchisor financing program is a material change in financing availability. The disclosed interest rate is a material financial term and was removed with the financing program.

8 atomic changes. The grant of an exclusive territory was replaced by an express non-exclusive territory with competition from other Area Representatives and franchisor-controlled channels. Territorial rights changed from unconditional continuation to a sales-volume condition with a termination right for development of additional units.

3 atomic changes. The franchisor's duty to protect IP reverses from no duty to a duty to protect and control litigation. A new right allows the franchisor to unilaterally modify materials and impose the cost on the franchisee.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. Introduction of a new covenant not to compete and confidentiality obligation for franchisees and business managers. The obligation changed from mandatory personal participation to allowing a fully trained and qualified manager to fulfill it, a material operational change.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 11 atomic changes. The consent exception to the non-compete was removed, making the restriction absolute. The explicit franchisor discretion to designate products as optional or mandatory was removed, altering the franchisee's obligation to sell authorized goods.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 15 atomic changes. The disclosed governing agreement changes from a Franchise Agreement to an Area Representative Agreement, reclassifying the relationship. The franchisee's expressly disclosed right to terminate under applicable state law is removed.

2 atomic changes. The franchisor broadened its no-financing disclosure from only the Development Fee and Initial Franchise Fee to any part of the initial investment in the Area Development Program. The disclosed upper bound of the Area Development Program total estimated initial investment increased by $500,000; this is a material revision to a disclosed estimate, though components are unchanged.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Expanded franchisee obligation from possible upgrade of cash register to mandatory purchase and installation of software, manuals, materials, and equipment; material cost/obligation change. Removal of franchisor's obligation to stock initial inventory is a clear operational assistance change.
1 atomic change. Per-meal payment to franchisee changed from a fixed $0.05 to a $0.05-$0.09 range, increasing the disclosed upper bound of franchisee compensation.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. New disclosure of a specific dollar amount of affiliate revenue from required purchases is a material disclosure change but does not alter franchisee obligations.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Removes explicit inclusion of refresher courses from post-opening training offer and attendance requirement. Adds a new timing obligation tying initial training completion to at least one week before opening.
1 atomic change. Removal of a disclosed statement about the conditions for continuation of franchise and territorial rights; a disclosure change with potential economic implications.
1 atomic change. Registration status of the proprietary marks changed from pending to registered, a clear legal status change.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Adds a contractual saving clause that preserves express FDD representations despite the integration clause.
1 atomic change. New disclosure adds a material limitation on the comparability of the FPR benchmark to a franchisee's cost structure.
4 atomic changes. Franchised outlet count increased from zero to four, a material operational change. The list of states with projected openings changed, with some states removed and others added.
1 atomic change. The new FDD adds audited financial statements for the full 2022 fiscal year to the previously disclosed inception and 2021 periods, a clear disclosure-coverage change.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. Introduces a new franchise type with a minimum store commitment and development schedule, materially expanding the offering. Item 1 no longer discloses a designated Protected Area for unit franchisees, a change in territorial right disclosure.

2 atomic changes. The removal of a disclosed executive position is a structural change in the management disclosure. The organizational structure of the top executive role changed from a combined President/CEO to a separate CEO, a clear operational change.
5 atomic changes. A new material fee with a defined formula is introduced in the new Item 5. A new material fee is introduced, albeit conditional on the franchisee's choice.

16 atomic changes. Additional on-the-job training after failing the food production test changed from no additional cost to $1,500 per week. A new Area Development Agreement fee formula was introduced in the 2025 Item 7.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 10 atomic changes. A new $10,000 fee was introduced for franchisees who do not use the designated design vendor. The design vendor requirement changed from mandatory to optional, altering franchisee choice and obligation.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. New designated exclusive provider relationship for esports leagues is introduced. Addition of full-time requirement for manager is a clear operational obligation change.
4 atomic changes. The per-location Area Development Fee doubled from $10,000 to $20,000. The initial franchise fee amount increased from $20,000 to $30,000, a material fee change.

2 atomic changes. Center royalty rate reduced from 8% to 6% of Net Sales, a material fee change. New explicit cap on mystery-customer evaluation fee assessments at once per quarter limits franchisor's fee assessment frequency.
9 atomic changes. The credit per location doubled, a material financial offset change. The area development fee per location doubled from $10,000 to $20,000.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Expanding the definition of Proprietary Products to include items used in operation broadens the franchisee's exclusive-purchase obligation. The Grand Opening Advertising Program now explicitly requires digital marketing services from designated vendors in addition to public relations services.
1 atomic change. Removal of guaranty obligation row from Item 9 table is a clear disclosure-method change, though underlying obligation status is unverified.

4 atomic changes. SBA consulting fee schedule changed from a single $2,500 flat fee (or 2%) to three program-specific flat fees, with two new higher fees. Monthly fee for a third-party retirement plan administration service increased by $10, a material fee change.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Adds a material termination and fee-forfeiture right for Studio franchisees who fail to open within the required period. Broadens the franchisee's obligation to provide video/camera feed access by removing the 'web-based' restriction.
1 atomic change. Changing a vague reasonable-period compliance obligation to a fixed 10-business-day deadline is a clear timing/obligation change.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 9 atomic changes. New pre-opening obligation to prepare site survey and construction plans for franchisor review and ensure ADA and code compliance is a material execution change. New right for the franchisor to update system standards in a confidential manual is a material discretion/control change.

4 atomic changes. Removal of franchisor's stated discretion to discount the initial franchise fee eliminates a potential cost-reduction avenue for certain franchisees. Material increase in the disclosed total cost range for the required outdoor inflatable amusement park purchase.
9 atomic changes. Indoor POS vendor changed from named vendors to a franchisor-approved vendor. New indoor inflatable park note imposes a 90-day ordering deadline after lease signing.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 13 atomic changes. Direct reversal of a disclosed benefit tied to supplier use, affecting the economic incentive structure for franchisees. New mandatory refurbishment obligation imposes significant potential costs on franchisees.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. The new FDD adds a disclosure of the time period franchises have been offered for each Riverside portfolio company, a new disclosure method. The number of affiliates offering franchises increased from 3 to 6, a material change in the disclosed corporate structure.

6 atomic changes. New Call Center Fee introduced with a minimum of $150 per month or 3% of Gross Sales, currently not imposed. New Liquidated Damages obligation introduced for termination due to franchisee default or wrongful termination, with formula based on royalty and brand fund fees.

4 atomic changes. Payee for the digital marketing fee changed from franchisor (or digital marketing company) to the designated digital marketing company directly. Newly disclosed recommended range of funds for a 1-year period after opening, $30,000 to $120,000.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. Maximum monthly technology fee cap increased from $400 to $750. New clause gives franchisor ownership of franchisee's business email and phone identity.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Renewal right changes from a contractual conditional right to a franchisor-discretionary offer, a material change in franchisee renewal security. The old disclosure expressly permitted further renewals by mutual agreement; the new disclosure omits this provision.
1 atomic change. The FPR qualifying outlet population materially increased from 43 to 55, changing the outlet universe for all performance statistics; this is a clear methodology/population change.
1 atomic change. The old and new FDDs disclose different system-wide 2024 franchised outlet termination counts (3 versus 4), a factual restatement in the required Item 20 status table.
1 atomic change. Adds a conditional refund right for the required inventory purchase, a clear operational/financial condition change benefiting the franchisee.

2 atomic changes. Introduces a specific new per-person fee obligation for national business meeting attendance. Adds a discretionary contractual right to increase a fixed monthly fee, materially altering the fee's potential burden.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. New mandatory insurance requirement imposes a material ongoing cost and obligation on franchisees. New minimum aggregate liability limit imposes a quantified floor on required coverage.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. Adds a broad disclosure that the franchisor faces no contractual restrictions in requiring upgrades or renovations, material to franchisee obligations. Specifies a material per-person fee for annual meeting attendance where the prior disclosure stated only an unspecified reasonable fee.

1 atomic change. Removal of a contractual assurance that the limited protected territory right is not subject to minimum sales requirements or other contingencies during the term is a material change to the conditionality of the franchisee's territory protection, increasing franchisor discretion.
1 atomic change. The Principal Mark changed from a pending application to a registered mark, a material change in trademark status.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. Franchisor discretion explicitly expanded to staffing, hours, and incentive-program participation. Mandatory product/sale scope changed from all System products to Manual-specified and designated required products.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 26 atomic changes. Disclosed ALL franchise count increased from 147 to 162. Disclosed Blue Moon franchise count increased from 91 to 124.
5 atomic changes. The mandatory standard initial fee decreased by $1,000 for the same standard PAR definition. The disclosed veteran discount increased from $2,000 to $5,000.
8 atomic changes. Cost for existing franchisee adding Textiles increased from $9,450 to $9,625. Estimated Equipment and Supplies costs increased substantially across all service line configurations.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. The administrative cost percentage on franchisor-obtained insurance dropped from 18% to 3%. The mandatory purchase list from the designated supplier was narrowed, but software licensing moved to the franchisor, changing the scope of required purchases.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The certification obligation changes from obtaining to obtaining and retaining, and now allows equivalent certification.

3 atomic changes. Removal of a named executive from Item 2 business experience disclosure is a clear disclosure change. Addition of a named executive to Item 2 business experience disclosure is a clear disclosure change.
